items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: Willy "the Lion" used to play there.

ctx.x: That's right. That's what they always say.

Fats Waller, Willy "the Lion", James B. [P.] Johnson, right on down the line. Corky -- there used to be a whole lot who never got much publicity, but a whole lot of them. They played stride piano. That's New York piano.
They always refer to James A. Johnson as the father of stride piano. Was he really the first? Weren't there others?

items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: But out of all those piano players, you know, I like Willy "the Lion's" style.

ctx.x: They always refer to James A. Johnson as the father of stride piano. Was he really the first? Weren't there others?

No. You know they put these names on people. You can't say who is who or what is what, way back to Scott Joplin. What the hell, I mean, you know, all these guys, they played, one copied from the other and the other copied from -- even now you have Fats Waller on a record and you're not sure it's Fats, you know. You say, "Yeah, that's Fats," and then you had Jimmy Johnson, you know. You know, playing about along the same lines. But out of all those piano players, you know, I like Willy "the Lion's" style. You…
sort of (Imitating piano). You know, that style. He plays a lot of things. Plus, he can -- look here, Willis "the Lion" plays "Carolina Shout," man, that's the classic all time great, you know. Yeah.
